messages:
maria.chen: FYI — we just got a DSAR that includes a record stored in the old SFTP archive (legacy-retention bucket). asking for full erase + proof of propagation. redacted identifier: <redacted@example.com>
jamal: ugh. that archive is encrypted with the old keystore `rw-legacy-key-v1` that we rotated last year. can someone confirm current key material still decrypts those snapshots? :eyes:
eli: I ran a quick check last week — we still have the master key in KMS but it was rewrapped. deletion should be possible, but we need to be careful: rotation policy removed direct IAM bindings on the key last quarter. ops will need a short-lived grant or we do a key-policy exception.
security-bot: auto-alert: retention-exception flagged for review (ticket #SE-9283). Please do not make permanent policy changes without documented approval. :warning:
ops-tom: I can grant a timebound IAM grant to `service-account:sftp-erasure@infra` for decrypt/describe only. request scope + duration? I suggest 4 hours unless legal asks for longer.
maria.chen: 4 hours sounds fine. legal-sara — what evidence do you need for the DSAR to be considered satisfied? audit logs? stdout of deletion job?
legal-sara: We need: 1) confirmation that data linked to requester ID was removed; 2) auditable deletion log entries (who ran it, when, which objects); 3) propagation check — any backups/snapshots and timelines. A signed statement from security/ops with job output attached is ideal.
jamal: on backups: the archive has periodic tar snapshots in `sftp-archive/snapshots/YYYYMMDD.tar.gz`. After we delete the matching files we must ensure subsequent snapshot generation does not restore them. For older snapshots we need to mark them for redaction or rotate keys and prove they are inaccessible, or perform targeted rewrite and re-upload.
eli: ops approach: create ephemeral IAM grant, run deletion script that does a safe pass (list -> verify -> delete) and writes structured JSON proof lines. example output: ```{
  "object": "sftp-archive/snapshots/20210103.tar.gz",
  "deleted_paths": ["users/redacted@example.com/msg1.txt"],
  "by": "service-account:sftp-erasure@infra",
  "ts": "2026-03-21T14:12:03Z"
}``` attach that to ticket. Also export KMS decrypt logs for the operation.
security-bot: note: KMS audit entries are in cloud-logs. retention for those logs is 2 years in prod by default. legal-sara: confirm if that meets the evidentiary requirement?
legal-sara: 2 years OK for now, but attach a signed retention-exception if we need to hold longer. For DSAR closure we don't require longer than 90 days of evidence availability.
maria.chen: two operational asks: (1) RBAC change: timeboxed grant to `sftp-erasure` for decrypt + object delete; (2) we need a retention-exception request to redact/change older snapshot policy if reupload/restore risk exists. ops-tom will file the grant and I'll file the retention-exception doc.
ops-tom: filing grant now. command we used (internal): `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding rw-legacy-key-v1 --member=serviceAccount:sftp-erasure@infra --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter --condition='timestamp < \"2026-03-21T18:30:00Z\"'`
jamal: quick vuln/triage note: do not broaden key access. keep scope minimal to the single service-account. after deletion, rotate customer-access wrappers and verify no leftover access paths.
maria.chen: agreed. tagging this for post-op audit: @eli to attach deletion JSON + KMS logs to ticket SE-9283 and @legal-sara to confirm wording for the signed statement. once legal signs off, we close DSAR. :thumbsup:
legal-sara: will draft the confirmation template; need the JSON + KMS logs by EOD.
eli: working on it now. I'll run deletion in the next 20min and push artifacts to the ticket.
security-bot: job update: erasure-job scheduled by ops-tom at 2026-03-21T14:05Z.
maria.chen: thanks team — keeping this thread as the single source for approvals and artifacts. will update ticket with the retention-exception request link when filed.
